angle: How explanation quality is MEASURED: XAI faithfulness/stability metrics, their use in security and networking, and evidence that the metrics themselves are unreliable or mutually inconsistent

papers.title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
papers.authors: Julius Adebayo, Justin Gilmer, Michael Muelly, Ian Goodfellow, Moritz Hardt, Been Kim
papers.relevance: Foundational model/data randomization tests showing several popular saliency methods are independent of both model and data; the sanity-check paradigm is the baseline test any traffic-classification explainer must pass.

papers.title: Evaluating the visualization of what a Deep Neural Network has learned
papers.authors: Wojciech Samek, Alexander Binder, Gregoire Montavon, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Klaus-Robert Mueller
papers.relevance: Origin of AOPC region-perturbation evaluation of heatmaps (pixel flipping), the ancestor of nearly every deletion-style faithfulness metric later applied to flow-feature attributions.

papers.title: A Benchmark for Interpretability Methods in Deep Neural Networks (ROAR)
papers.authors: Sara Hooker, Dumitru Erhan, Pieter-Jan Kindermans, Been Kim
papers.relevance: ROAR (RemOve And Retrain) evaluation showing many attribution methods are no better than random feature designation; retraining avoids the OOD confound of naive deletion metrics.

papers.title: RISE: Randomized Input Sampling for Explanation of Black-box Models
papers.authors: Vitali Petsiuk, Abir Das, Kate Saenko
papers.relevance: Introduced the deletion and insertion AUC metrics that became a de facto standard for causal faithfulness evaluation of importance maps.

papers.title: ERASER: A Benchmark to Evaluate Rationalized NLP Models
papers.authors: Jay DeYoung, Sarthak Jain, Nazneen Fatema Rajani, Eric Lehman, Caiming Xiong, Richard Socher, Byron C. Wallace
papers.relevance: Defines sufficiency and comprehensiveness, the two faithfulness metrics most often ported from NLP rationales to feature attributions in other tabular/sequence domains including security.

papers.title: Towards Faithfully Interpretable NLP Systems: How should we define and evaluate faithfulness?
papers.authors: Alon Jacovi, Yoav Goldberg
papers.relevance: Conceptual hub separating faithfulness from plausibility and arguing for graded rather than binary faithfulness evaluation; frames what any traffic-classifier explanation metric is actually measuring.

papers.title: The (Un)reliability of saliency methods
papers.authors: Pieter-Jan Kindermans, Sara Hooker, Julius Adebayo, et al.
papers.relevance: Shows attributions change under input transformations that do not change the model output (input invariance failure), an early demonstration that explanation methods themselves are unreliable.

papers.title: Interpretation of Neural Networks is Fragile
papers.authors: Amirata Ghorbani, Abubakar Abid, James Zou
papers.relevance: Adversarial perturbations that keep predictions fixed but radically change saliency/DeepLIFT/relevance explanations; motivates stability as a mandatory evaluation axis for security explainers.

papers.title: On the Robustness of Interpretability Methods
papers.authors: David Alvarez-Melis, Tommi S. Jaakkola
papers.relevance: Introduces local Lipschitz stability metrics for explanations and shows LIME/SHAP-style methods score poorly; the stability metric reused by security XAI evaluations (Fan et al., xNIDS).

papers.title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Metrics
papers.authors: Richard Tomsett, Dan Harborne, Supriyo Chakraborty, Prudhvi Gurram, Alun Preece
papers.relevance: Applies psychometric reliability analysis to fidelity metrics themselves and finds saliency metrics are statistically unreliable and mutually inconsistent - a key 'metrics are broken' result.

papers.title: The Disagreement Problem in Explainable Machine Learning: A Practitioner's Perspective
papers.authors: Satyapriya Krishna, Tessa Han, Alex Gu, Javin Pombra, Shahin Jabbari, Steven Wu, Himabindu Lakkaraju
papers.relevance: Formalizes and measures disagreement between post-hoc explainers (rank agreement, top-k overlap) and documents that practitioners resolve conflicts with ad hoc heuristics.

papers.title: The Disagreement Problem in Faithfulness Metrics
papers.authors: Brian Barr, Noah Fatsi, Leif Hancox-Li, Peter Richter, Daniel Proano, Caleb Mok
papers.relevance: Directly shows that the faithfulness metrics used to arbitrate between explainers do not agree with one another on tabular data, leaving practitioners without a trustworthy referee - exactly the meta-level inconsistency this corpus needs.

papers.title: Quantus: An Explainable AI Toolkit for Responsible Evaluation of Neural Network Explanations and Beyond
papers.authors: Anna Hedstroem, Leander Weber, Dilyara Bareeva, et al.
papers.relevance: The standard open-source library implementing 30+ explanation-quality metrics (faithfulness, robustness, localization, complexity, randomization); the practical instrument for any traffic-classification XAI evaluation.

papers.title: The Meta-Evaluation Problem in Explainable AI: Identifying Reliable Estimators with MetaQuantus
papers.authors: Anna Hedstroem, Philine Bommer, Kristoffer K. Wickstroem, Wojciech Samek, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Marina M.-C. Hoehne
papers.relevance: Because quality estimators disagree and there is no ground truth, proposes meta-evaluating the metrics themselves via resilience to noise and reactivity to randomness; the canonical 'evaluate the evaluators' paper.

papers.title: A Consistent and Efficient Evaluation Strategy for Attribution Methods (ROAD)
papers.authors: Yao Rong, Tobias Leemann, Vadim Borisov, Gjergji Kasneci, Enkelejda Kasneci
papers.relevance: Information-theoretic analysis showing perturbation masks leak class information (a confounder that produces conflicting metric rankings); ROAD debiases removal and cuts cost ~99% vs ROAR.

papers.title: On Pitfalls of RemOve-And-Retrain: Data Processing Inequality Perspective
papers.authors: Junhwa Song, Keumgang Cha, Junghoon Seo
papers.relevance: Proves ROAR scores can be inflated by information-free post-processing (blurring) of attribution maps, i.e. the benchmark rewards properties unrelated to explanation quality.

papers.title: Decoupling Pixel Flipping and Occlusion Strategy for Consistent XAI Benchmarks
papers.authors: Stefan Bluecher, Johanna Vielhaben, Nils Strodthoff
papers.relevance: Shows attribution rankings from occlusion-based faithfulness benchmarks flip depending on the occlusion strategy (studied across 40 variants) and proposes strategy-decoupled metrics (R-OMS/SRG).

papers.title: Normalized AOPC: Fixing Misleading Faithfulness Metrics for Feature Attribution Explainability
papers.authors: Joakim Edin, Andreas Geert Motzfeldt, Casper L. Christensen, et al.
papers.relevance: Demonstrates AOPC is model-sensitive and misleading for cross-model comparison and proposes a normalization; directly relevant when comparing explainers across different traffic classifiers.

papers.title: F-Fidelity: A Robust Framework for Faithfulness Evaluation of Explainable AI
papers.authors: Xu Zheng, Farhad Shirani, Zhuomin Chen, et al.
papers.relevance: Diagnoses OOD and information-leak problems in ROAR-style fidelity evaluation and proposes explanation-agnostic fine-tuning with random masking; validated on time series as well as image/text.

papers.title: A Fresh Look at Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
papers.authors: Anna Hedstroem, Leander Weber, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Marina M.-C. Hoehne
papers.relevance: Shows the Model Parameter Randomisation Test itself has methodological confounds (noise, layer order, similarity measure) and proposes Smooth/Efficient MPRT - a metric-repairing-a-metric paper.

papers.title: Revisiting Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
papers.authors: Gal Yona, Daniel Greenfeld
papers.relevance: Argues the randomization sanity-check methodology itself conflates task artifacts with method failures, undermining conclusions drawn from the most-cited XAI evaluation test.

papers.title: Do Feature Attribution Methods Correctly Attribute Features?
papers.authors: Yilun Zhou, Serena Booth, Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Julie Shah
papers.relevance: Dataset-modification procedure that induces ground-truth feature importance, then shows saliency/rationale/attention methods frequently fail to recover it; template for ground-truth evaluation in traffic datasets with planted features.

papers.title: Synthetic Benchmarks for Scientific Research in Explainable Machine Learning (XAI-Bench)
papers.authors: Yang Liu, Sujay Khandagale, Colin White, Willie Neiswanger
papers.relevance: Synthetic tabular benchmark suite where conditional expectations (and thus ground-truth attributions) are computable exactly, enabling metric-vs-metric comparison; tabular setting maps directly onto flow-feature traffic classifiers.

papers.title: Ground Truth Evaluation of Neural Network Explanations with CLEVR-XAI
papers.authors: Leila Arras, Ahmed Osman, Wojciech Samek
papers.relevance: Controlled VQA testbed with ground-truth relevant regions for benchmarking ten heatmap methods; the model for building selective, controlled, realistic ground-truth XAI benchmarks.

papers.title: "Will You Find These Shortcuts?" A Protocol for Evaluating the Faithfulness of Input Salience Methods for Text Classification
papers.authors: Jasmijn Bastings, Sebastian Ebert, Polina Zablotskaia, Anders Sandholm, Katja Filippova
papers.relevance: Plants known shortcuts in training data so ground-truth salience is known, then shows popular method configurations fail to find them; the planted-shortcut protocol transfers naturally to synthetic traffic traces.

papers.title: OpenXAI: Towards a Transparent Evaluation of Model Explanations
papers.authors: Chirag Agarwal, Dan Ley, Satyapriya Krishna, et al.
papers.relevance: Open benchmark implementing eleven quantitative metrics spanning faithfulness, stability and fairness of post-hoc explanations, mostly on tabular data - directly reusable for flow-feature NIDS/traffic models.

papers.title: A Causal Lens for Evaluating Faithfulness Metrics
papers.authors: Kerem Zaman, Shashank Srivastava
papers.relevance: Causal Diagnosticity testbed comparing faithfulness metrics via model-editing-derived pairs of faithful/unfaithful explanations; finds most metrics perform near chance and diagnostic power varies by task - fresh evidence metrics are unreliable.

papers.title: Toward Understanding the Disagreement Problem in Neural Network Feature Attribution
papers.authors: Niklas Koenen, Marvin N. Wright
papers.relevance: Simulation study with known data-generating processes explaining WHY attribution methods disagree, showing scaling choices and evaluation metrics generate inconsistent method rankings.

papers.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Interpretability Methods through Explanation Invariance and Equivariance
papers.authors: Jonathan Crabbe, Mihaela van der Schaar
papers.relevance: Formal robustness metrics (invariance/equivariance under model symmetries) with theoretical guarantees; a principled alternative to ad hoc stability measures.

papers.title: "Is your explanation stable?": A Robustness Evaluation Framework for Feature Attribution (MeTFA)
papers.authors: Yuyou Gan, Yuhao Mao, Xuhong Zhang, et al.
papers.relevance: Security-venue framework quantifying explanation uncertainty with statistical guarantees and defining stability-adjusted faithfulness metrics; bridges XAI-metric research and the security community.

papers.title: On the Effectiveness of Methods and Metrics for Explainable AI in Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification
papers.authors: Jonas Klotz, Tom Burgert, Begum Demir
papers.relevance: Domain-transfer study (remote sensing) explicitly finding that faithfulness metrics inherit the same OOD-perturbation problems as the perturbation methods they score; a caution for porting metrics to traffic data.

papers.title: A Dual-Perspective Approach to Evaluating Feature Attribution Methods
papers.authors: Yawei Li, Yang Zhang, Kenji Kawaguchi, et al.
papers.relevance: Argues existing faithfulness evaluations are flawed and decomposes faithfulness into soundness and completeness, two complementary measurable properties.

papers.title: Investigating sanity checks for saliency maps with image and text classification
papers.authors: Narine Kokhlikyan, Vivek Miglani, Bilal Alsallakh, Miguel Martin, Orion Reblitz-Richardson
papers.relevance: Shows sanity-check conclusions from images do not transfer to text and depend on input-multiplier and smoothness properties - evidence that metric verdicts are modality-dependent (relevant when applying them to packet/flow inputs).

papers.title: Benchmarking Perturbation-based Saliency Maps for Explaining Atari Agents
papers.authors: Tobias Huber, Benedikt Limmer, Elisabeth Andre
papers.relevance: Combines sanity checks and insertion-style input degradation to benchmark five perturbation explainers in RL, illustrating how the metric toolbox is assembled in a non-image domain.

papers.title: Evaluating Explanation Methods for Deep Learning in Security
papers.authors: Alexander Warnecke, Daniel Arp, Christian Wressnegger, Konrad Rieck
papers.relevance: THE hub for this corpus: defines security-specific evaluation criteria (descriptive accuracy, sparsity, completeness, stability, efficiency, robustness) and benchmarks six explainers on malware/NIDS/vulnerability models.

papers.title: LEMNA: Explaining Deep Learning based Security Applications
papers.authors: Wenbo Guo, Dongliang Mu, Jun Xu, Purui Su, Gang Wang, Xinyu Xing
papers.relevance: First high-fidelity explainer purpose-built for security models (RNN-based binary analysis, network data); introduced fidelity testing via feature deduction/augmentation (PCR) that later security XAI evaluations reuse.

papers.title: DeepAID: Interpreting and Improving Deep Learning-based Anomaly Detection in Security Applications
papers.authors: Dongqi Han, Zhiliang Wang, Wenqi Chen, et al.
papers.relevance: Interpretation framework for unsupervised anomaly detection (incl. Kitsune network traffic) evaluated on fidelity, stability, robustness and efficiency - the security-domain instantiation of XAI quality criteria.

papers.title: xNIDS: Explaining Deep Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems for Active Intrusion Responses
papers.authors: Feng Wei, Hongda Li, Ziming Zhao, Hongxin Hu
papers.relevance: Explains DL-NIDS by capturing feature dependencies of structured flow data and explicitly evaluates explanations on fidelity, sparsity, completeness and stability against prior methods - the closest sibling to XAI-for-traffic-classification evaluation.

papers.title: Can We Trust Your Explanations? Sanity Checks for Interpreters in Android Malware Analysis
papers.authors: Ming Fan, Wenying Wei, Xiaofei Xie, Yang Liu, Xiaohong Guan, Ting Liu
papers.relevance: Ports the sanity-check idea to security: defines quantitative stability, robustness and effectiveness metrics and shows popular interpreters (LIME etc.) give seed-dependent, unstable explanations for malware classifiers.

papers.title: AI/ML for Network Security: The Emperor has no Clothes (TRUSTEE)
papers.authors: Arthur S. Jacobs, Roman Beltiukov, Walter Willinger, Ronaldo A. Ferreira, Arpit Gupta, Lisandro Z. Granville
papers.relevance: Generates high-fidelity, low-complexity, high-stability decision-tree 'trust reports' for network-security ML (incl. traffic classifiers) and uses them to expose shortcut learning and spurious correlations in published models - explanation quality operationalized as fidelity+complexity+stability for networking.

papers.title: SoK: Explainable Machine Learning for Computer Security Applications
papers.authors: Azqa Nadeem, Daniel Vos, Clinton Cao, et al.
papers.relevance: Systematization of ~300 XAI-for-security papers; documents that explanation evaluation in security is largely absent (only 14% do user studies) and most works do not validate explanation correctness at all.

papers.title: E-XAI: Evaluating Black-Box Explainable AI Frameworks for Network Intrusion Detection
papers.authors: Osvaldo Arreche, Tanish Guntur, Jack W. Roberts, Mustafa Abdallah
papers.relevance: End-to-end framework evaluating SHAP and LIME on NIDS models across three datasets with six explanation-quality metrics (descriptive accuracy, sparsity, stability, efficiency, robustness, completeness) - the Warnecke criteria applied wholesale to network traffic.

papers.title: A Critical Assessment of Interpretable and Explainable Machine Learning for Intrusion Detection
papers.authors: Omer Subasi, Johnathan Cree, Joseph Manzano, Kevin Barker
papers.relevance: Empirically documents that post-hoc explainers yield inconsistent influential features across methods for the same IDS models and questions the whole feature-attribution pipeline for intrusion detection.

papers.title: Good-looking but Lacking Faithfulness: Understanding Local Explanation Methods through Trend-based Testing
papers.authors: Jinwen He, Kai Chen, Guozhu Meng, Jiangshan Zhang, Congyi Li
papers.relevance: Security-venue paper showing visually plausible explanations fail trend-based faithfulness tests; evaluates ten explainers including on security tasks, separating 'looks right' from 'is faithful'.

papers.title: Explainable AI for Forensic Analysis: A Comparative Study of SHAP and LIME in Intrusion Detection Models
papers.authors: Pamela Hermosilla, Sebastian Berrios, Hector Allende-Cid
papers.relevance: Recent head-to-head of SHAP vs LIME on XGBoost/TabNet intrusion detectors measured on fidelity, consistency and relevance - one of the few applied networking papers that actually quantifies explanation quality.

papers.title: Explainable AI for Intrusion Detection Systems: LIME and SHAP Applicability on Multi-Layer Perceptron
papers.authors: Diogo Gaspar, Paulo Silva, Catarina Silva
papers.relevance: Validates LIME/SHAP explanations of an MLP-based IDS through perturbation analysis - representative of the partial, perturbation-only evaluation style common in applied NIDS work.

papers.title: A Lightweight, Efficient and Explainable-by-Design Convolutional Neural Network for Internet Traffic Classification (LEXNet)
papers.authors: Kevin Fauvel, Fuxing Chen, Dario Rossi
papers.relevance: Explainable-by-design CNN for traffic classification claiming 'faithful explainability' by construction - the design-side answer to unreliable post-hoc metrics, and a direct XAI-for-traffic-classification datapoint.

papers.title: Dos and Don'ts of Machine Learning in Computer Security
papers.authors: Daniel Arp, Erwin Quiring, Feargus Pendlebury, et al.
papers.relevance: Canonical pitfalls paper for ML evaluation in security (sampling bias, spurious correlations, inappropriate baselines); frames why explanation-quality evaluation in NIDS inherits broken experimental practice.

papers.title: Explainable Intrusion Detection Systems (X-IDS): A Survey of Current Methods, Challenges, and Opportunities
papers.authors: Subash Neupane, Jesse Ables, William Anderson, et al.
papers.relevance: Survey of explainable IDS that repeatedly flags the absence of standardized explanation-quality evaluation as an open challenge in the field.

papers.title: Recent Applications of Explainable AI (XAI): A Systematic Literature Review
papers.authors: Mirka Saarela, Vili Podgorelec
papers.relevance: Review of 512 applied XAI studies finding most rely on anecdotal evidence or expert opinion rather than quantitative explanation-quality metrics - quantifies the evaluation gap this corpus targets.

papers.title: Local Explanation Methods for Deep Neural Networks Lack Sensitivity to Parameter Values
papers.authors: Julius Adebayo, Justin Gilmer, Ian Goodfellow, Been Kim
papers.relevance: Companion result to the sanity checks: explanations of trained and random-weight networks are visually similar, attributed to architectural priors - early warning that visual assessment misleads.

papers.title: Adversarial attacks and defenses in explainable artificial intelligence: A survey
papers.authors: Hubert Baniecki, Przemyslaw Biecek
papers.relevance: Survey of attacks that manipulate explanations (and fairness metrics) without changing predictions; adversarial manipulability is the security-relevant failure mode of explanation metrics.

papers.title: Manipulation Risks in Explainable AI: The Implications of the Disagreement Problem
papers.authors: Sofie Goethals, David Martens, Theodoros Evgeniou
papers.relevance: Shows that because many 'valid' explanations exist for one prediction (disagreement), providers can cherry-pick explanations - turns metric inconsistency into a security/audit threat model.

papers.title: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Intrusion Detection Systems
papers.authors: Maonan Wang, Kangfeng Zheng, Yanqing Yang, Xiujuan Wang
papers.relevance: Widely-cited SHAP-on-NSL-KDD IDS explanation paper; the archetype of apply-SHAP-without-evaluating-it work that the faithfulness-metrics literature critiques.

general_xai: ERASER suite (Movies, e-SNLI, FEVER, MultiRC, CoS-E, BoolQ, Evidence Inference)
SST-2 / IMDB / AG News for text faithfulness
synthetic tabular data with known data-generating process (XAI-Bench, Koenen & Wright simulations, Bastings planted shortcuts)
security_networking: nPrint OS-fingerprinting and published traffic-classification artifacts re-audited by TRUSTEE

recurring_explanation_methods: Gradient/saliency, Gradient x Input, SmoothGrad, Integrated Gradients, GradCAM, Guided Backprop
LIME and KernelSHAP/DeepSHAP/TreeSHAP (dominant in security/networking applications)

security-specific explainers: LEMNA (fused-lasso mixture regression), DeepAID (optimization-based for unsupervised models), xNIDS (history-input sampling with feature-dependency capture), TRUSTEE (surrogate decision trees)
recurring_models: MLPs, XGBoost, Random Forest, TabNet on tabular flow features (E-XAI, Hermosilla, Gaspar, Barr)
RNN/LSTM sequence models for binary analysis and NIDS (LEMNA, xNIDS)
1D-CNNs on packet bytes for traffic classification (Fauvel LEXNet)
recurring_metrics: model/data parameter randomization tests (MPRT and its Smooth/Efficient repairs)
AOPC / pixel flipping / deletion & insertion AUC
ROAR retraining and ROAD debiased removal
Lipschitz/local stability; rank agreement & top-k feature agreement (Krishna)
security-domain six-pack: descriptive accuracy, sparsity, completeness, stability, efficiency, robustness (Warnecke -> E-XAI -> xNIDS lineage)
author_stated_limitations: Tomsett et al. (1912.01451): applying psychometric reliability tests shows saliency fidelity metrics are 'statistically unreliable' and inconsistent across calculation choices - i.e., the metrics themselves fail sanity checks.
Barr et al. (2311.07763): faithfulness metrics 'lack agreement with one another' on tabular data, 'leaving practitioners uncertain' which metric to trust when choosing an explainer.
Krishna et al. (2202.01602): 'state-of-the-art explanation methods often disagree'; practitioners resolve conflicts with 'ad hoc heuristics', risking reliance on misleading explanations.

Rong et al. (ROAD, 2202.00449): the shape of the perturbation mask leaks class information, a confounder that produces 'conflicting rankings' between evaluation strategies; ROAR-style retraining is also ~99% more expensive than needed.

Song et al. (2304.13836): via the data-processing inequality, ROAR scores can be inflated by information-free blurring of attribution maps - removal benchmarks are 'biased toward spatially blurry masks'.
Bluecher et al. (2401.06654): benchmark outcomes flip with the occlusion strategy (40 variants tested); rankings are an artifact of the removal design unless metric and occlusion are decoupled.
Edin et al. (NAOPC, 2408.08137): 'AOPC is sensitive to variations in the model, resulting in unreliable cross-model comparisons' - lower AOPC may reflect the model, not the explanation.
Hedstroem et al. (Fresh Look, 2405.02383): the original MPRT's layer order, similarity measure and noise sensitivity bias its verdicts; even the most-used sanity check needed repair.
Yona & Greenfeld (2110.14297): sanity-check failures can reflect task artifacts rather than method flaws; 'fundamental difficulties in evaluating saliency maps beyond visual inspection' remain.
Hedstroem et al. (MetaQuantus, 2302.07265): with no ground truth, competing quality estimators disagree, motivating meta-evaluation by 'resilience to noise and reactivity to randomness'.

Zaman & Srivastava (2502.18848): under a causal testbed most faithfulness metrics perform near chance and 'diagnostic performance varies across tasks and models'; continuous metrics beat their binarized versions.

Zhou et al. (2104.14403): even with induced ground truth, saliency/rationale/attention methods often fail to recover known-important features; recommend validating any new method against controlled ground truth before deployment.

Bastings et al. (2111.07367): 'some of the most popular method configurations provide poor results' even on planted, easy-to-find shortcuts; hyperparameters of the explainer matter as much as the method.
Jacovi & Goldberg (2004.03685): the community conflates plausibility with faithfulness; binary faithfulness claims are untenable, argue for 'graded' evaluation criteria.
Klotz et al. (2507.05916): 'faithfulness metrics share the same problems as perturbation-based methods' - the OOD artifacts of perturbation contaminate the metric as much as the explainer.
Kokhlikyan et al. (2106.07475): sanity-check conclusions drawn on images 'do not transfer' to text models - metric verdicts are modality-dependent, cautioning direct reuse on network data.

Warnecke et al. (1906.02108): generic XAI criteria are insufficient for security; even among six methods there are 'significant differences' and some popular methods (LIME/SHAP-style) are unstable and slow for security workloads.
Fan et al. (2008.05895): existing interpreters for Android malware give seed-dependent, non-robust explanations; stability/robustness/effectiveness must be measured before analysts can trust them.
Subasi et al. (2407.04009): different explainers yield 'inconsistent influential features' for the same IDS model; recommend inherently interpretable models and cross-explanation consistency checks.
Nadeem et al. (SoK, 2208.10605): only ~14% of XAI-for-security studies conduct any user evaluation; explanation correctness is mostly asserted, not measured.
Saarela & Podgorelec (app14198884): across 512 applied XAI studies 'most rely on anecdotal evidence or expert opinion rather than robust quantitative metrics'.
He et al. (2309.05679): explanations can be 'good-looking but lacking faithfulness' - visual plausibility diverges from measured fidelity on security tasks.

Jacobs et al. (TRUSTEE): post-hoc explanations must jointly optimize fidelity, complexity and stability to be usable by network operators; applying TRUSTEE revealed shortcut learning and spurious correlations in multiple published network-security models, i.e., prior evaluations missed underspecification.
Zheng et al. (F-Fidelity, 2410.02970): ROAR-style retraining leaks explanation information into the retrained model and naive removal causes OOD; evaluation must be explanation-agnostic.
Gan et al. (MeTFA, 2209.01782): 'explanation algorithms are vulnerable to adversarial attacks' and single-run faithfulness scores are noisy; metrics need statistical significance guarantees.
Goethals et al. (2306.13885): explanation multiplicity lets providers cherry-pick favorable explanations - the disagreement problem becomes a manipulation/audit risk.
Baniecki & Biecek (2306.06123): explanations and even fairness/quality metrics can be adversarially manipulated; defenses are immature.
notes.synthesis_for_angle: The general lesson of this sub-literature: (1) there is a mature toolbox of faithfulness/stability metrics (randomization tests, AOPC/deletion-insertion, ROAR/ROAD, sufficiency/comprehensiveness, Quantus implementations); (2) a substantial 2019-2025 strand shows these metrics are mutually inconsistent, confounded (OOD, class leakage, occlusion-strategy dependence, model sensitivity) and sometimes near-chance diagnostically, spawning meta-evaluation (MetaQuantus, Causal Diagnosticity) and repaired metrics (ROAD, NAOPC, sMPRT/eMPRT, F-Fidelity); (3) the security/networking community imported the metrics via Warnecke->Fan->DeepAID->xNIDS->E-XAI using a fairly stable six-criteria vocabulary, while TRUSTEE reframed quality as fidelity+complexity+stability of surrogate trees for network models; (4) applied traffic-classification/NIDS papers overwhelmingly apply SHAP/LIME without any quality evaluation (documented by SoK Nadeem, Saarela, Neupane), which is precisely the gap an XAI-for-traffic-classification study can fill - but it must confront the metric-unreliability results in (2), ideally with planted-ground-truth traffic data (Bastings/Zhou/XAI-Bench style) rather than perturbation metrics alone.
